standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the representing object for the cohomological functor considered in the proof, which is the first half of the argument.

standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that representing the functors of the form Hom(F(-), Y) by objects of the source yields a right adjoint.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of an adjoint
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the adjoint obtained is exact, which is the second assertion.

core_obligations: The representing candidate (proof lines 3028-3036): for an object Y of the target the author considers the functor sending an object W to the group of morphisms from its image under the given functor to Y, observes that it is cohomological because the functor is exact and transforms direct sums into direct sums, and applies the representability lemma to represent it by an object X of the derived category.

The adjoint and its exactness (proof lines 3037-3041): the existence of the right adjoint follows from the criterion on representable functors, and exactness of that adjoint is the cited exactness result.
proof_roadmap: Exhibit Hom(F(-), Y) as a cohomological functor and represent it.
Apply the criterion for the existence of an adjoint.
Cite the exactness of the adjoint obtained.
difficulty_reason: The proposition states that an exact functor of triangulated categories from the derived category of a Grothendieck abelian category which transforms direct sums into direct sums has an exact right adjoint (statement lines 3020-3026). The proof is a complete argument: for a fixed target object the author shows that the functor sending an object to the group of morphisms from its image under the given functor into that object is cohomological, because the given functor is exact and preserves direct sums, and represents it by an object of the derived category using Brown representability (proof lines 3028-3036); the criterion on representable functors then gives the right adjoint and the cited result gives its exactness (proof lines 3037-3041). The non-formal content is the identification of the functor to be represented. The claim is H2.
